blocks.text: Anti-tampering protection prevents non-admin end users from stopping, modifying, and deleting Zscaler products, services, files, and Windows registry keys. Admins can enable or disable anti-tampering in Zscaler Client Connector App Profiles. To disable anti-tampering as an end user, see Troubleshooting Zscaler Client Connector.
Anti-tampering is supported only on Windows and macOS desktop operating systems. It is not supported on Windows Server operating systems.
Anti-tampering is available for Zscaler Client Connector versions 4.1 and later for Windows and Zscaler Client Connector versions 5.0 and later for macOS.
Zscaler Anti-Tampering does not run in safe mode by design. Zscaler recommends disabling safe mode for all end users and allowing safe mode access only to the administrator.

blocks.item: The anti-tampering framework is part of the Zscaler Endpoint Protection (ZEP) module and is installed by the ZEPInstaller.exe installer, a 32-bit program on a 32-bit OS or a 64-bit program on a 64-bit OS, that is embedded as a resource inside the Zscaler Client Connector installer. For example, Zscaler-windows-4.0.60.9-installer.exe.
The ZEP module is installed only when anti-tampering is enabled using an install option. To learn more, see Supported Parameters for Zscaler Client Connector for Windows.
The Zscaler Client Connector installer unpacks the ZEPInstaller.exe to /programfiles/zscaler on the local hard drive.
The anti-tampering framework is part of the ZEP module, which is bundled with the Zscaler Client Connector .pkg installer.
The ZEP module is installed only when anti-tampering is enabled using an install option. To learn more, see Supported Parameters for Zscaler Client Connector for macOS.
The Zscaler Client Connector installer installs the anti-tampering package /Applications/Zscaler/ZEP.app and other related components, such as the ZEP system extension, on the local hard drive.

blocks.text: You can disable anti-tampering by doing one of the following:

blocks.item: Turning off Enable Anti-tampering option in App Profiles. To learn more, see Configuring Zscaler Client Connector App Profiles.
Providing a one-time password (OTP) in the Zscaler Client Connector app. To learn more, see Troubleshooting Zscaler Client Connector in the Modern UI.
Disabling the anti-tampering install parameter in the property list (PLIST) configuration settings. This is only available for Zscaler Client Connector for macOS.
